requirements_inventory.summary: GET /health returns {"status":"ok"}, and a page shows that status (the page is the frontend's part; this backend plan covers the endpoint).

stack.summary: Proposed: Node.js (>=18) using only the built-in http module, with no third-party dependencies. The target directory is empty and neither the requirements nor the configuration name a stack. A dependency-free Node server is the simplest common option for a single JSON endpoint: nothing to install, it starts fast, and unit tests run with the built-in node:test runner.

milestones.title: Health endpoint
milestones.goal: Add a runnable Node.js HTTP server whose GET /health endpoint returns {"status":"ok"} as JSON, and document it in openapi.json.

tasks.title: Project scaffold
tasks.description: Create package.json (name, private, "type": "commonjs", scripts: start = "node server.js", test = "node --test") with no dependencies, so that `npm install` succeeds as a no-op.

tasks.title: HTTP server with GET /health
tasks.description: Create app.js, which exports a request handler, and server.js, which listens on process.env.PORT (default 8000) at host 127.0.0.1. GET /health answers 200 with Content-Type application/json and the body {"status":"ok"}. Any other path answers 404 with a JSON error body {"error":"not found"}. Any other method on /health answers 405 with a JSON error body and an Allow: GET header. Every response carries Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *, so a separately served status page can fetch the endpoint.

tasks.title: OpenAPI document
tasks.description: Create openapi.json (OpenAPI 3.0.3) that documents only GET /health, with a 200 response whose application/json schema is an object with a required string property `status` (enum ["ok"]) and example {"status":"ok"}.

tasks.title: Unit tests
tasks.description: Add test/health.test.js using node:test. It starts the handler on an ephemeral port and checks that GET /health returns 200 with the JSON body {"status":"ok"}, and that an unknown path returns 404.

acceptance_criteria.text: GET http://127.0.0.1:8000/health responds with status 200, a Content-Type header starting with application/json, and a body that parses as JSON equal to {"status":"ok"}.
The GET /health response includes the header Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *, so a status page served from another origin can read it.
GET http://127.0.0.1:8000/does-not-exist responds with status 404 and a JSON error body.
openapi.json is a valid OpenAPI 3 document whose paths contain exactly one operation, `get` on /health, with a 200 application/json response schema that has the property `status`.

assumptions.text: The "page shows that status" part of HEALTH-1 is a frontend concern and will be built by a frontend step. This backend plan covers only the GET /health endpoint. It adds a permissive CORS header so that page can call the endpoint from another origin.
The server listens on 127.0.0.1, on port 8000 by default, and the PORT environment variable can override the port. The requirements do not specify a host or port.
The stack is proposed (dependency-free Node.js >= 18) because the target directory is empty and neither the requirements nor the configuration name a stack.
A 404 for unknown paths and a 405 for non-GET methods on /health are reasonable defaults. They do not add to the requirement or change it.
